items.title: Charles "Creole Charlie" Levy Interview, 1962-01-03
items.q: I think he was right on the corner, right on the, what's that, Pete Lalo? Yes.

ctx.x: Is that so? Yeah, I sneaked in there. Where'd you hear Joe play? Do you remember that?

I think he was right on the corner, right on the, what's that, Pete Lalo? Yes. I remember him and then. Corner place near the station, huh? Yeah, it was, what was it, Iperville Street? It was where the district was. I wasn't supposed to be there, but I sneaked in. And I had two three kids. One of them was studying saxophone, a couple of them studying violin, and one was studying bass. We were all interested, crazy about music, you know. And oh yeah, we used to go down the, halfway down the stairs there, they did…

Well, yeah, La Rocca and Shields. Yeah, Shields, yes. And Munez might have been. Munez, yeah, yes it was. Yeah, Yellow Munez. There was a fellow by the name of Gussie, Gussie, what was his name, was the trombone for a while. And the piano player was Ragus. Yes, that's right. Now, those fellows, when they came north, shifted around a little bit. They did, they had a choral.
